also: take good care of your health

evidence: Cic. Fam. 7.15.2, closing a letter (Lewis & Short s.v. cūrō)
Traupman 19: take care (of yourself), tē cūrā
terms.comment: Lewis & Short gives sē cūrāre, to look after oneself, refresh oneself (Ter. Ad. 5.1.1; Cic. Phil. 9.3.6), but not as a leave-taking, which is Cūrā ut valeās.

phrases.latin: «Cūrā ut valeās, mī fīlī,» inquit avia.
phrases.english: “Take care of yourself, my son,” said Grandma.
phrases.source: Libellus VI, Reditus: per Alpēs domum

phrases.english: Take good care of your health!

sources: Lewis & Short: valeo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 16–17, 19, 94, 287.
